# Generated Files — Keep vs. Untrack (decision record)

Status: **decided** (Aug 2026) — the generated files are **not committed**. They are gitignored and
regenerated on demand by the build/publish tooling.

## The files

| Generated file                                     | Source(s)                                                 | Regenerated by                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `core/chrome/utils/updater/updater-config.sys.mjs` | `config/installer.conf` (via `generateUpdaterConfig.mjs`) | `createZip.mjs` at publish time (ships inside `utils.zip`)      |
| `tools/publish/remote-ui/updater.css`              | `installer/web/style.css` + `tools/publish/updater.css`   | `createZip.mjs` at publish time (ships inside `updater-ui.zip`) |
| `installer/src/_config.h`                          | `config/installer.conf`                                   | installer Makefile `config` target (every build, `FORCE` rule)  |
| `installer/src/resources.h`                        | `installer/web/*` (via `installer/embed.mjs`)             | installer Makefile `resources` target (every build)             |

All four are `#include`d / imported by the consumers: `platform.h` includes `_config.h`, `main.c`
includes `resources.h`, the updater imports `updater-config.sys.mjs` from `utils.zip`, and the
updater tab links `updater.css` from `updater-ui.zip`.

## The question

Why commit them at all? Two reasons used to justify tracking:

1. **Self-contained C build** — a fresh `git clone && make` must compile without Node. But the
   Makefile already regenerates both C headers with `node` on every build (`embed.mjs`,
   `syncGeneratedFiles.mjs`), so Node is required to build regardless. The committed copies added
   nothing to a fresh-clone build.
2. **Pinned zip content / hash** — `updater-config.sys.mjs` ships inside `utils.zip` and its bytes
   drive the update detector. But `createZip.mjs` regenerates it from `installer.conf` at import
   time, _before_ zipping and hashing, so the zip always ships the config that matches the current
   publish run.

Meanwhile the cost of tracking was real:

- **Diff noise** — `resources.h` is a gzip byte-array; a one-line CSS change re-encodes the whole
  stream (~1.4k-line diffs for a single-line edit).
- **Hook machinery** — pre-commit / pre-push / post-rewrite hooks + `install-githooks.mjs` +
  `core.hooksPath` wiring, all to keep three derived files in sync with their sources on every git
  operation (`--no-verify`, rebases, amends).
- **Publish gate** — `upload.mjs` had to verify committed-vs-fresh before every prod publish.

## Decision: untrack + generate on demand

The generated files are gitignored and produced exactly when something needs them:

- `make dist_win` / `dist_linux` / `dist_mac` → Makefile regenerates `_config.h` (+ `resources.h`)
  on every build, with the current `MODE`/`LOCAL` URLs.
- `upload` / `upload:local` → `createZip.mjs` regenerates `updater-config.sys.mjs` on import, before
  hashing and zipping.
- By hand → `node tools/publish/syncGeneratedFiles.mjs` (or `node installer/embed.mjs`).

The git hooks, `tools/install-githooks.mjs`, the `prepare` script, and the prod sync gate in
`upload.mjs` are deleted.

### Pros / cons

| Criterion                         | Committed (before)                                  | Untracked + on-demand (now)                                             |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fresh-clone C build               | works (files present)                               | works — Makefile regenerates them with node                             |
| Node required to build            | yes (Makefile already ran node)                     | yes (same)                                                              |
| Diff noise (`resources.h`)        | large gzip diffs on every UI change                 | none — the file is gitignored                                           |
| Git-hook machinery                | pre-commit/pre-push/post-rewrite + `core.hooksPath` | none                                                                    |
| Publish gate (committed vs fresh) | `checkSync()` + `git diff --quiet HEAD`             | none — publish regenerates what it needs                                |
| Change detection (hashes)         | derived from the generated files on disk            | ✓ only after the hash rework (below) — otherwise updates silently break |
| Risk                              | drift if hooks bypassed                             | must keep hash inputs correct (rework below)                            |

## The trap: change detection must cover the true sources

The publish hashes were computed over **on-disk files filtered by gitignore**. The generated files
lived inside the hashed trees and were the _proxies_ for "did the inputs change":

- `resources.h` carried `installer/web/*` changes into the installer hash (`web/` was not even in
  the installer source set).
- `_config.h` carried `installer.conf` changes into the installer hash.
- `updater-config.sys.mjs` carried config changes into the **utils** hash and the zip content.

Simply `git rm` + gitignore would silently drop all three from `getAllFiles()` — config/UI changes
would stop bumping hashes, users would never get new installers/zips, and a fresh clone (no files on
disk) would hash differently from a dev machine (files present). The rework re-points every hash/zip
at the true sources:

### Packages (`utils`, `fx-folder`)

- `utils` hash and manifest `files` list now **explicitly add back**
  `updater/updater-config.sys.mjs` (untracked) via `computeDirectoryHash(dir, patterns, extraFiles)`
  in `tools/publish/hashUtils.mjs` — and `createZip` adds the same file to `utils.zip` via its new
  `extraFiles` parameter. The file is regenerated by `createZip.mjs` before hashing, so the zip,
  hash and manifest always agree, and a config change still bumps the utils hash.
- `updater-ui` hash and manifest `files` list **explicitly add back** `updater.css` (untracked) the
  same way; `createZip` regenerates it before hashing and adds it to `updater-ui.zip`.
- `fx-folder` has no generated files — unchanged.

### Installer binary

- The installer hash now uses `computeFileSetHash(entries)` over a labeled set spanning
  `installer/src` (minus `helper/`), `installer/web/*` and `config/installer.conf` — the true
  sources of the generated headers. A UI or config change still triggers a rebuild.
- The helper hash is unchanged (`installer/src/helper`).
- The installer hash has no published `files` list, so the runtime hash check is unaffected.

### Runtime hash check (installer + in-browser updater)

Unchanged by design: it hashes the **installed** directory against the manifest's `files` list.
Because the list now includes `updater/updater-config.sys.mjs` (which ships in the zip and lands in
the installed profile), the published and local hashes stay in agreement.

## Updater UI moved into its own shipped package

Firefox 155 removed the ability to embed srcdoc/data:/blob: frames in a system-principal chrome
document, which broke the remote-UI iframe approach (`REMOTE_UI_URL` + postMessage bridge) for good.
The updater tab UI therefore stopped being a hosted page and became a third package,
`updater-ui.zip`, shipped and hash-checked like the others:

- `tools/publish/remote-ui/updater.html` + `updater.js` (engine) + `updater-ui.js` (client) +
  generated `updater.css` + `logos/` → `updater-ui.zip` → `chrome/utils/updater/ui` →
  `chrome://firefox-scripts/content/ui/*`.
- `scriptsUpdater.sys.mjs` (utils.zip) downloads + verifies + extracts `updater-ui.zip` before
  opening the tab (`ensureUpdaterUi`).
- `REMOTE_UI_URL`, `buildRemoteUiBlobs`, the iframe/postMessage bridge and the `LOCAL` config flag
  were removed; `updater.css` became a generated file that ships in the zip (row above).

## What developers must know

- Never hand-edit the generated files; edit `config/installer.conf` / `installer/web/*` /
  `tools/publish/updater.css` and let the tooling regenerate.
- The Makefile and publish scripts regenerate on demand; no git hooks, no sync gate.
- `upload` deletes the generated files from disk when it finishes (`cleanGenerated` in
  `syncGeneratedFiles.mjs`, called from `upload.mjs`'s `finally`), so a local/dev run never leaves
  localhost/dev-baked copies around — the working tree ends up exactly like a fresh clone. A `make`
  build regenerates them; a later `upload` regenerates them again.
- `pnpm lint` / `pnpm format` skip the gitignored files (prettier respects `.gitignore`; the
  generator output is prettier/clang-format clean).
- If you change a generator's _inputs_, the corresponding hash changes and the next `upload`
  rebuilds/re-publishes — verify with `pnpm upload:local -- --mode=prod` and
  `node installer/test/test_hash.mjs`.

Historical note: `core/chrome/utils/updater/update.css` was an earlier generated file, removed when
the updater UI first moved to a hosted page; `updater.css` (in `tools/publish/remote-ui/`) is its
successor and now ships inside `updater-ui.zip`. Nothing generated is committed anymore.
